title: Human Egg Cell Anatomy: Oocyte Layers & Ovulation Guide
description: Learn human egg cell anatomy, including the secondary oocyte, zona pellucida, corona radiata, cortical granules, polar bodies, and full ovulation timeline.
h1: Human Egg Cell (Oocyte) Anatomy, Layers and Ovulation Guide
blurb: Inside one of the body's largest cells: the secondary oocyte, protective zona pellucida, nourishing corona radiata, cortical granules, and ovulation timing.
lead: Spanning roughly 120 micrometers across, the human oocyte is one of the largest cells in the body and carries the cytoplasmic machinery needed to begin a new life. In this illustrated guide to human egg cell anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including oogonium, primary oocyte, meiosis i completion, secondary oocyte—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Spanning roughly 120 micrometers across, the human oocyte is one of the largest cells in the body and carries the cytoplasmic machinery needed to begin a new life. An oocyte begins development before birth as a primary oocyte arrested in meiosis I. During a reproductive cycle, an LH surge triggers completion of meiosis I in a selected follicle; ovulation releases a secondary oocyte arrested in meiosis II, surrounded by zona pellucida and corona radiata. Meiosis II usually finishes only after sperm entry, creating the ovum and another polar body. The follicle becomes a progesterone-secreting corpus luteum. A secondary oocyte in this teaching cutaway has no large resting central nucleus; the small polar body is outside the oocyte membrane but inside the zona. This is a stylized microscopic-scale model, not an actual ovum photograph. questions.question: Is the egg released at ovulation already a mature ovum?
questions.answer: Typically the released cell is a secondary oocyte arrested in meiosis II, not a completed ovum. Meiosis II normally finishes only after sperm entry.

questions.question: What surrounds the ovulated human oocyte?
questions.answer: An extracellular zona pellucida surrounds its plasma membrane, and granulosa-derived corona radiata cells surround the zona. These structures are distinct from the ovarian follicle wall left behind.

questions.question: What is the first polar body?
questions.answer: The first polar body is a small cell produced by unequal division during oocyte meiosis I; it may lie in the perivitelline space and is not a second egg.

questions.question: When do human primary oocytes form?
questions.answer: Primary oocytes arise before birth in the fetal ovary and remain arrested in meiosis I until selected cycles years later. In a typical cycle an LH surge precedes the final preovulatory meiotic transition.

questions.question: What happens to the follicle after ovulation?
questions.answer: The follicle remnant becomes a corpus luteum that produces progesterone and estrogen. If implantation follows, early trophoblast hCG helps maintain that luteal hormone support.
